# Copilot instructions

These rules apply to every Copilot agent and contributor working on Polaris, so that the agents of @aschauera and @KlausThyri build the same game. The documentation holds the details: [game design](../docs/game-design.md), [architecture](../docs/architecture.md), [roadmap](../docs/roadmap.md) and the [README](../README.md). This file and the documentation must never contradict each other.

## Working order: issues, blocked-by and stacked PRs

- Work starts from a GitHub issue. Before picking one, check its **Relationships** in the sidebar: start only issues whose *blocked by* issues are all closed, and do not implement a blocked issue early as part of another change.
- GitHub allows *blocked by* relationships only between issues, not between pull requests. So every PR closes its own issue (`Closes #N` in the description), and the issues carry the order. When new work builds on unmerged work, create an issue for it and mark it blocked by the issue of that work: sidebar → Relationships → *Mark as blocked by*, or `gh api -X POST repos/aschauera/polaris-game/issues/<N>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<database id of the blocker>`.
- A PR that builds on another unmerged PR is **stacked**: its base is that PR's branch, and its description states the merge order. Merge in *blocked by* order. When a base PR merges and its branch is deleted, GitHub retargets the next PR to `main`. Closing keywords only take effect for PRs that target `main`, so check that the issue closed after the merge.
- Issue texts can be older than the current contracts. Briefs 8–14 (#9–#15), for example, were written for the square grid and generator 2. Where an issue contradicts the documentation or this file, the documentation and this file win; correct or annotate the issue when you notice.
- The [current package-to-issue map](../docs/roadmap.md#existing-dependencies-and-legacy-issues) supersedes the old first-playable issue sequence, including the original waves in parent #5. Save reliability #35 merged through #47; all P2/#36 prerequisites are closed as of 12 November 2026. P2 implements the shared-landmass scenario/player scaffold; G2/#63 adds preview-only island maps and blocks P3a/#52. P3 combat/victory precedes workers/research; P3a adds boats and playable island crossings. Diplomacy/AI remain later. #12 was folded into P3/#10, not implemented separately. Check live relationships before starting; documenting or creating an issue does not authorize its blocked gameplay.
- **Approved generator-first extractions:** G1/#53 added canonical water depth, irregular submerged banks and matching rendering/inspection before combat. G2/#63 adds deterministic home/beacon island layouts and a topology selector, independent of combat and boats. P3a/#52 depends on #10, #53 and #63. Neither generator package adds Landing/Harbour, water movement or playable island starts.

## Keep docs and agent guidance in sync

- A PR that changes rules, visuals, architecture, workflow or deployment updates the affected documentation **and** this file in the same PR. A decision that lives only in a chat, a PR comment or one person's local instructions is not binding for the other agent: write it down here or in the docs.
- Before finishing, search this file, the README and `docs/` for statements your change makes stale: grid shape, rules and generator versions, references, palette, controls, test counts and captures. Fix them in the same PR.
- Record each decision with its reason where it belongs: architecture ADRs for technical decisions, game design for rules and visuals, roadmap for scope and order, README for setup, controls and verified evidence.

## Game and multiplayer decisions

- **Canonical English documentation:** [game design](../docs/game-design.md#target-status-and-baseline) owns the full implemented/target rules, lore, tribes/catalogs, economy and decision register; [architecture](../docs/architecture.md#planned-target-domain-and-compatibility) owns technical deterministic-domain/messenger/version/save contracts; [roadmap](../docs/roadmap.md#detailed-target-delivery-plan) owns the complete dependent packages, acceptance and testing. Integrate changes there, not in parallel main documents. The complete foundation #20 → #21 → #22 → #24 → #29 → #31, design #33/#34 and save reliability #47 are integrated into main at `c6c4cad`; preserve those contracts. Do not merge/retarget PRs merely to document them, or present the planned target gameplay as implemented.
- **Planned gameplay is not implemented:** three common counter-classes (Bulwark > Assault > Breaker > Bulwark), combat, beacon activation/victory, city conquest and explicit end conditions come before full tribal content. P2 already provides two-player slots, independently chosen presentation-only tribes, validated shared-landmass starts, public reserved beacons and later-founder production. Amazons, Raccoons, Engineers and Sorceresses replace Meridian/Lantern only in new versioned content; six-resource economics, workforce, hunger, supply and bounded abilities are planned. Numeric balance and remaining ability/content choices stay provisional; do not present test values as verified balance. Never reinterpret old saves under the new design.
- **Confirmed target decisions:** PvP starts at war; diplomacy is optional later. Both players choose tribes independently, including mirrors from the start; ownership and research belong to player IDs, not tribe IDs. There is no city-count cap: spacing (initial test value 4 hex steps), supply and expensive founders constrain expansion. P2 grants one free founder and scout per player and makes later founders production decisions. The current prototype has no faction-wide stockpile; neither player receives one, and city-local food/materials start at zero on founding. Military food debt is accepted for the first iteration. Civilians can be killed only through an explicit adjacent attack consuming the attack action, with no automatic movement kill, loot, conversion, retreat or prisoner subsystem; city fortifications and then civilian occupancy must be cleared before atomic takeover. P2 validates the shared-landmass configuration; separate home islands and beacon islands follow in P3a (E15) using baseline reachability (land plus connected shallow-water routes through a common Landing), room, contestable beacons and travel-turn fairness, rejecting failing maps instead of repairing them. Water crossing is common production, never research: the proposed P3a rule uses shallow/shoal for ordinary boats and shelf/deep for deep-water-capable boats, normally enabled by a Harbour; bathymetry and underwater sandbanks create irregular routes, not a fixed coast-distance radius. A Landing is needed to embark initially; a unit retains its vessel ashore and can re-embark elsewhere. These rules (E17) and per-tribe water styles (E18) remain proposals; styles need both maintainers' approval and never carry map validation. Movement is never research-gated: hills cost 2 from the start.
- **Research and staged content:** Stockpiling → Cultivation Methods, Roadbuilding → City Planning, Metalworking → Equipment, Resonance Measurement → Resonance Engineering. One project per player faction, fixed faction baseline plus staffed knowledge buildings, retained per-technology progress on switching, no research theft through conquest. Basic food/wood/stone/simple metal, all three base classes and beacon activation need no research. Housing unlocks precede population 4/7 territory gates. Research F1 depends on P7, before complete P8, never on P11; the first isolated combat/victory slice needs no research. Diplomacy/AI are not first-match blockers. Initially implement one characteristic ability per tribe; full catalogs remain expansion goals. Test six mixed and four mirror pairings with swapped starts.

- The board is a **pointy-top hex grid** in odd-r offset rows with six neighbours (`src/game/hex.ts`; neighbour order east, south-east, south-west, west, north-west, north-east). Canonical tile IDs stay `z * width + x`. Rules are **version 5**, scenario **version 2**, generator **version 6**.
- **Direct orders and availability.** Tap/click an own unit or its hex to select it; show only that unit's affordable domain range, then move immediately on a reachable destination tap. Scouts have 4 movement points; founders, guards and workers have 2. All units and cities provide radius-2 sight; refresh the incoming faction's unit budgets on its turn. A static voxel diamond above the figure (a cut gem in clear ice white with cyan facets, no faction colour; part of the cached figure mesh, no halo or extra mesh) marks own units with a legal move, and a subtle static plate glow marks own cities with an empty production queue, only while the viewer may act. Tap a city/name plate to select production; occupied queues do not glow. City plates and held beacon plates share one compact 20 px plate style with a 44 px invisible touch band. Keep controls keyboard-accessible and distinguish pan/pinch from taps. No combat, worker improvements or roads are added. Retain readable older-rule saves unchanged, just as older-generator saves; reject incompatible replay.
- Gameplay is deterministic ([ADR-002](../docs/architecture.md#adr-002-deterministic-domain)): integer arithmetic, explicit PRNG state, stable order. A change that alters generated maps or rule outcomes bumps the generator version or `RULES_VERSION`; messenger turns of another version are rejected with a reason.
- Generator-v4 bays are real, ocean-connected water, not cosmetic holes in land. Keep broad separated landmasses, warped shores and deep curved inlets on sufficiently large forms. Never silently reinterpret older-generator matches: retain their stored records, clear only their auto-resume pointer and explain the incompatibility.
- **Canonical water depths (G1/#53) and G2 island layouts (#63):** generator v6 preserves the shared-landmass generator-v5 data while adding the seed-derived archipelago topology, with home and beacon islands shaped before tile classification. Both topologies use the same canonical water-depth classes; routes are validated from generated shallow/shoal cells, never forced by post-generation repair. Include topology and depth in `mapHash`; retain incompatible v3–v5 saves unchanged. Rules remain v5. Archipelago maps are preview-only until P3a/#52 adds boats and water movement.
- **Scenario (#36/#63):** scenario v2 preserves validated shared-landmass starts and adds a preview-only archipelago layout. Validate both-start access to every beacon over generated shallow/shoal water, mirrored travel-turn fairness, coastal city sites, beacon neighbours and two further legal city sites per home; reject unsuitable maps without terrain repair. Messenger envelopes carry scenario version, topology and two tribe IDs; placements rebuild from the seed. Readable scenario-v1 turns and generator-v3–v5 saves are retained and rejected with a compatibility reason. Tribes remain presentation-only, and later founders are a production choice only while city capacity remains.
- Authoritative rules live in `src/game`, without DOM or Babylon. Rendering and UI consume snapshots and submit commands; they never resolve rules.
- Multiplayer is **play by messenger** ([ADR-005](../docs/architecture.md#adr-005-serverless-play-by-messenger)): players exchange turn links, codes or files, and each copy replays the command log. The server-authoritative online variant (#17, #23) was discarded. Do not add a server, relay or WebRTC without a new decision recorded in the architecture.
- **Save and transport reliability.** Report failed storage writes explicitly, keep warnings separate from transient sharing notices, and never shelve or switch away from an unsaved match, including when a known older message selects another match. Explicit Leave remains the discard path. Set auto-resume only after saving; report pointer/removal/migration failures. Clear a match's own auto-resume pointer before deleting its record so failed pointer cleanup leaves a recoverable save. Messenger commands use the existing 10,000-order transport cap and reserve the last slot for End turn; solo rules and replay hashes are unchanged. Keep readable over-limit local archives byte-for-byte and listed, clear only their own auto-resume pointer, reject replay and prevent incoming turns from overwriting retained records. Local archive parsing must not relax incoming limits.

## Validation

Run `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test:unit` and `npm run test:e2e` before handing over; CI runs them on every push and pull request. Report the actual results and any limitations in the PR.

## Azure deployment

Deploy Polaris as an **Azure Container App**, not a static website or App Service.
Local setup provisions or reuses Azure resources; the Container App is configured
for built-in GitHub continuous deployment. Azure generates the GitHub Actions
workflow and secrets; the Azure-generated workflow is maintained in this repo.
GitHub builds the root Dockerfile and deploys **only when a GitHub release is
published**, after validating its tagged commit. Pushes, tag pushes, drafts and
manual dispatches must not deploy. Do not replace this with local image builds
or another deployment workflow. Keep the release workflow on the default branch;
Azure setup regenerates push triggers, so do not rerun bootstrap setup against a
release-managed app.

Keep both Azure setup scripts interactive by default: list existing resources
at each resource-selection step and include a **(new)** option. Preserve explicit
parameters, `-NonInteractive`, and side-effect-free `-WhatIf` for automation.
Subscriptions are an existing-account prerequisite, not resources these scripts
create. See [deployment documentation](../README.md#docker-and-azure-container-apps)
and run `pwsh -File .\scripts\azure-setup.tests.ps1` after script changes.

## Graphics rules for the hex voxel world

Details and numbers are in [ADR-004](../docs/architecture.md#adr-004-map-and-rendering) and the [visual direction](../docs/game-design.md#visual-and-interaction-direction). Binding rules:

- **Hex fields of cubic voxels.** Land hexes stack soil, dirt or rock cliffs and a grass, sand or rock top. Hills form low connected elevation terraces, never a separate grassy cone or tall pillar on every hex. Keep the four detailed land levels at 0.625, 0.75, 0.875 and 1 world units; coarse voxels may merge levels instead of exaggerating heights. Water hexes contain a stepped voxel seabed under a level translucent surface, with blue diorama cut walls. No hexagonal voxels, smoothed terrain, decorative image textures or imported models.
- **Voxel density.** Overview densities are 16 voxels across a hex up to 32, then 8 up to 64, 4 up to 128 and 2 above. Zoom restores up to 16 in one padded, chunk-aligned camera window, never a full high-density 256² map. Anchor CPU noise and shader cells to global columns; reuse overlapping chunks. Maximum map dimensions remain 256 per side. Scale decorations in world units; keep counts sparse. The three overview fixtures retain a 900k vertex ceiling; active detail windows have separate bounds in ADR-004.
- **A calm, readable board**, as in *Into the Breach*: few elements per hex, and smaller trees on the back row, so the centre stays free for a unit. Detailed trees are at most 0.75 world units high with narrower crowns; simplify them at coarse scales without clipping settlements. Terrain identity must not rely on colour alone. Both land and water caps use visible, crisp screen-space hex hairlines that fade when zoomed out; the earlier open-water suppression is superseded. Preserve pixel-aware edge coverage, not broad blurry strokes; selection, reachable outline and territory border stay distinct and readable.
- **Voxel water and readable coasts.** Build four broad underwater terraces from canonical water depths and sparse seeded coastal rock groups, both fully submerged and emerging through shallow water. Keep their world-space depths independent of fine voxel density; do not restore ten or more microsteps. Use compact, irregular voxel lobes, not tall thin pillars; exposed grey rock displaces the cap in its footprint and participates in actual-height picking while remaining a water tile. A flat plane with square shading or colour bands is not a substitute. Show pale sand in the shallows, muted stone at the shelf and deep blue farther out. Never recompute depth from fog or camera state: a charted water hex's depth is observed terrain and remains fixed when neighbouring land is revealed. Only charted neighbours shape coastal rocks/highlights and land beaches; unknown hexes expose no depth, geometry, picks or labels. Keep all four cap colours and inspection names even where coarse floors merge. Planned P3a navigation uses shallow/shoal for ordinary boats and shelf/deep for deep-water-capable boats; fine decoration never changes a tile's class. Draw water hexes only on the level cap, not on submerged floors; range and territory overlays remain land-only. Classify every seabed palette kind as water floor and keep terrain/water shader-cache variants distinct. Share chunk geometry between opaque and transparent submeshes; no per-cube meshes, refraction or continuous wave animation. See ADR-004 for exact heights and coarse-scale merging.
- **Irregular sandbanks.** Lower broad sandy pockets inside existing land hexes so they occupy areas and physically interrupt cliffs; never substitute a painted narrow rim. Vary their width, retaining intact cliffs between them. Only charted water can shape a bank. Keep whole trunk footprints on their charted tile and off sand, use sparse stones rather than tufts, and preserve level settlements and dry land-resource sites. Meshing, picking, figures and marker positioning share actual ground heights; refresh markers after coastal remeshing. Banks do not change domain terrain/elevation, land/water identity or movement. See ADR-004 for heights and coarse-scale omission.
- **Visual resources, not new rules.** Stone deposits, apple groves and fish shoals share a seeded presentation classifier for geometry, original projected SVG annotations and inspection names. Stone deposits are broad irregular grey blocks with different flat cap heights, chipped shoulders and occasional rubble, not repeated narrow towers; keep the tile centre clear for units. No `Tile` mutation, simulation RNG, harvesting, yields or movement change. Only charted occurrences may be exposed; remembered ones are dimmed and settlements suppress them. Use the existing projected label layer, with camera-bounded candidates, at most 128 visible resource nodes, overview culling and cleanup on regeneration/disposal; no extra per-resource WebGL objects. The inspector must state that harvesting is not available.
- **Voxel lighthouses for public beacons (#56, #58).** A charted beacon levels and clears its tile like a city site (`BEACON_SITE`, bit 0 clear, so no keep), with a small irregular paved plaza at fine scales, and shows one cached lighthouse of finest 1/16 voxels set back 0.15 units from the hex centre; a unit on the beacon steps forward and stays readable. Keep the tower, including banners, inside its hex. A neutral tower has a pale white lantern, terracotta bands, no banner and a plain ivory marker; never use gold for neutral, because gold is Meridian's colour. A held tower shows its holder's colour in lantern and bands, banners on the camera-facing gallery sides and a faction-coloured marker plate naming the holder; the banner tail (Meridian swallowtail, Lantern point) and the named plate keep ownership readable without colour. Holders are public: show them on uncharted markers and on dimmed remembered towers. Until P5 (#15) stores holders, only the `?diagnostics=1` preview may set them, and it must never change commands, saves, turns or the state hash. The lantern glow is static (unlit full-brightness voxels; no light source, bloom or animation). Uncharted beacons show only their public marker above uniform fog; remembered ones are dimmed. Towers are non-pickable separate meshes rebuilt with exploration/detail and disposed with regeneration; their materials are created lazily and shared by every look, so beacon-free scenes keep the tested mesh/material budgets. The map atlas previews the same three neutral lighthouses where `createScenario` forms a fair match for that seed and size (#60), and none otherwise; the status line names the result. They change no placement, movement or rule.
- **Shaded surfaces, not flat fills.** Use deterministic world-anchored light/dark patches with five shade levels, broader 2-by-2-voxel water cells and one-voxel ground cells. Fade fine contrast in the overview and soften it at the shoreline. These shades supplement real underwater geometry; never replace it. Keep fog uniform and overlays readable; no extra image textures or geometry. Static shades stay anchored; the separately throttled water glints below are the sole animation exception.
- **Clear territory**, as in *Polytopia*: a faction-coloured border band on the inner edge of each territory, and a name plate with the population above each visible city. Selection is a gold hex outline; hexes reachable this turn get their own outline. Keep the three distinct.
- **Chunky voxel figures**, as in *Voxel Tactics*: units are small voxel figures in faction colours, standing on their hex. No sprites or billboards.
- Learn from these games' design; never copy their art, names or assets.
- **Palette.** The world uses `VOXEL` in `src/rendering/voxels.ts`: reference yellow-green grass, cyan shallows, saturated deep blue, pale sand, warm earth, grey stone, forest/olive foliage and terracotta roofs. Calibrate actual framebuffer colours after shading/blending, not raw hex values; preserve the reference-median and thin-grid regressions in `tests/atlas.spec.ts`. Shallow/shoal/shelf/deep cap colours share one transparent material and consume the charted hex's canonical depth; never replace the real underwater relief with colour bands. The Art Deco navy, teal, gold and ivory palette is for the HUD and UI; gold also marks focus and city plates.
- **Fog.** Uncharted hexes are opaque and uniform and hide terrain, trees, resources, figures, picks and tooltips. Remembered hexes are dimmed; visible hexes are bright.
- **Camera.** Fixed orthographic camera, yaw 45°, pitch `atan(1/sqrt(2))` (about 35.264°), no rotation: cube axes project symmetrically at 30°, matching the concept's isometric reading. This is a geometric calibration, not recovered camera metadata from the illustration. Keep camera, screen-aligned tree placement, figure facing and picking tests on the shared basis in `src/rendering/view.ts`. Movement buttons retain their six relative screen directions; hex edges are no longer forced vertical/horizontal on screen.
- **Performance.** Terrain is meshed in chunks, never one mesh per hex. Explored dimming, ranges and borders update through state textures; newly charted terrain remeshes affected chunks. Scene changes call `invalidate()`. The sole animation exception is sparse world-anchored sun glints on visible water caps, throttled to an 80 ms minimum idle-frame interval. Keep the highlights translucent and restrained, with at most a 35% sun-colour blend and sparse per-cycle selection (`0.003 + 0.04 * gust`), not bright white flashes. Glints add no geometry, do not refresh shadows, stop for reduced motion, far overviews or no resident visible water, and never affect remembered water or simulation RNG. Static availability diamonds and plate glows require no animation. Stay within the tested resource bounds.
- Deferred concept elements (resource harvesting and further kinds, rivers and bridges, danger markers, palms, fields and harbours) are listed in the [roadmap](../docs/roadmap.md); add them through their own issues. Voxel boats and Landing piers are planned with P3a (#52), the Harbour with P8.

## Visual review delivery

Whenever visual changes are requested, implement them first, then capture fresh screenshots or other suitable visuals from the updated, running application for human inspection. Deliver these in a separate **Visual overview**, distinct from the implementation summary, with directly viewable visuals or links. Show the actual implemented result, not the reference image, a mockup, or stale screenshots. If fresh visuals cannot be captured, explicitly state the limitation and its cause.

For documentation screenshots, record the source commit, capture date, seed/map dimensions, viewport/DPR and browser/renderer environment in the [README provenance section](../README.md#current-verification-and-screenshot-provenance). Fresh successful CI captures are valid running-app evidence; copy them into the documentation before temporary artifacts expire and identify simulated failure states. Keep current captures distinct from the two immutable references and historical performance measurements.
